validation.notes: Repaired packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts (one line): DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions() called settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(true), so the pre-trust bootstrap ran with project settings and project-local extensions/packages enabled. It now forces untrusted (setProjectTrusted(false)) before settingsManager.reload() and before the package manager resolves extensions, regardless of the previously held trust state; reload() then re-applies the trust decision returned by resolveProjectTrust, so user/global and temporary CLI extensions still participate in the trust decision and are loaded. Regression (.prale-eval/regression.mjs) drives the real class through .prale-eval/subject.mjs's createTrustSubject boundary fakes (settings/package/extension loaders) and asserts on the observed event log and loader state: (1) with initialTrusted=true the very first event is ['set', false] and the following settings reload and package resolve both observe untrusted state, proving the bootstrap no longer inherits trusted state; (2) no 'extensions' load during the bootstrap pass contains project.ts while pre-trust extensions are exactly cli.ts + user.ts (user/global and CLI remain available); (3) a second reload of the now-trusted loader again starts with ['set', false] and resolves untrusted; (4) the resolved decision is honoured afterwards (project.ts appears only when trust is granted, and never when it is denied). Each case also asserts the state observed inside the resolveProjectTrust callback. Verified locally: exit 0 on the repaired source, and exit 1 with AssertionError 'bootstrap must force untrusted settings first, but the first event was ["set",true]' (event log showing project.ts loaded pre-trust) when the original setProjectTrusted(true) line is restored, then restored the fix. The repo's vitest suites could not be run as a supplementary check because no node_modules are installed and installing dependencies is out of scope; the only executed validation is the VM-module regression above, plus the fact that the same run loads and evaluates the complete TypeScript module, so the file parses and type-strips cleanly.
